docs.title: First-Principles, HPC & AI for Materials Discovery
docs.text:
Welcome to the Computational Materials Science Workshop.

This workshop provides a comprehensive introduction to modern computational approaches for materials discovery by integrating:

  • First-Principles Calculation
  • Density Functional Theory (DFT)
  • High Performance Computing (HPC)
  • Accelerated Materials Simulation
  • Artificial Intelligence for Materials Discovery

Start Workshop

Computational Workflow

docs.title: Workshop Overview
docs.text:
Computational Materials Science combines theoretical modeling, numerical simulation, and advanced computing technologies to understand, predict, and design new materials with targeted properties.

Through this workshop, participants will explore the complete computational workflow starting from material structure preparation, electronic structure calculation, atomistic simulation, and AI-assisted materials modeling.

docs.title: Why Computational Materials Science?
docs.text:
Traditional materials discovery requires extensive experimental exploration.

Computational approaches provide powerful tools to:

  • Predict material properties before experiments
  • Understand atomic-scale mechanisms
  • Accelerate materials discovery
  • Reduce computational and experimental costs
  • Support data-driven materials research

docs.title: Scientific Workflow
docs.text: Material Design ↓ Crystal and Molecular Structure Building ↓ First-Principles Calculation ↓ Electronic Structure Analysis ↓ Accelerated Atomistic Simulation ↓ Machine Learning Potential ↓ High Performance Computing ↓ Materials Discovery

docs.title: 01 Computational Materials Science
docs.text:
Introduction to the fundamental concepts of computational materials research:

  • Materials modeling principles
  • Structure-property relationships
  • Computational approaches in materials science
  • Materials discovery workflow

docs.title: 02 First-Principles Calculation
docs.text:
Learning electronic structure calculations using quantum mechanical approaches.

Topics include:

  • Density Functional Theory (DFT)
  • Kohn-Sham equation
  • Exchange-correlation functional
  • Pseudopotential
  • Geometry optimization
  • Electronic properties analysis

Main computational tool:

Quantum ESPRESSO

docs.title: 03 Accelerated Materials Simulation
docs.text:
Introduction to efficient simulation methods for larger material systems.

Topics include:

  • Density Functional Tight Binding (DFTB+)
  • Accelerated electronic structure calculation
  • Large-scale molecular simulation
  • Structure optimization workflow

docs.title: 04 Machine Learning for Materials Discovery
docs.text:
Application of artificial intelligence approaches in computational materials science.

Topics include:

  • Machine Learning Potential
  • Atomic environment representation
  • Training dataset preparation
  • AI accelerated molecular simulation

Example workflow:

MACE Machine Learning Potential

docs.title: 05 High Performance Computing Environment
docs.text:
Understanding computational infrastructure for large-scale simulation.

Topics include:

  • Linux computational environment
  • HPC architecture
  • Parallel computation
  • Job submission workflow
  • Simulation data management

docs.title: Software Environment
docs.text:
The workshop introduces several computational tools:

Software Application Quantum ESPRESSO First-Principles and DFT Calculation DFTB+ Accelerated Atomistic Simulation MACE Machine Learning Potential HPC Cluster Large Scale Computational Simulation Python Tools Data Processing and Analysis

docs.title: Expected Learning Outcomes
docs.text:
After completing this workshop, participants will be able to:

  • Explain the fundamentals of computational materials science
  • Understand first-principles calculation workflows
  • Perform basic Quantum ESPRESSO simulations
  • Understand accelerated simulation approaches using DFTB+
  • Apply machine learning concepts for materials modeling
  • Utilize HPC environments for computational research

docs.title: Target Participants
docs.text:
This workshop is intended for:

  • Researchers
  • University lecturers
  • Graduate students
  • Undergraduate students with computational interests
  • Materials science and engineering professionals

Participants are expected to have basic knowledge of:

  • Physics
  • Chemistry
  • Materials science
  • Engineering
  • Scientific computing

docs.title: Workshop Case Study
docs.text:
During the hands-on session, participants will apply computational workflows to investigate material systems through:

Structure Design → Simulation → Analysis → Materials Discovery

The case study integrates:

  • Atomic structure preparation
  • First-principles calculation
  • Computational simulation
  • AI-assisted materials modeling

docs.title: From Material Design to Materials Discovery
docs.text: This workshop introduces a complete computational workflow for materials discovery, starting from atomic structure preparation to advanced simulation and artificial intelligence approaches.

docs.title: Overall Workflow
docs.text: Material Design ↓ Atomic Structure Construction ↓ First-Principles Calculation ↓ Electronic Structure Analysis ↓ Accelerated Atomistic Simulation ↓ Machine Learning Potential ↓ High Performance Computing ↓ Materials Discovery

docs.title: Step 1: Material Design
docs.text:
The first step involves designing and preparing the target material system.

Activities include:

  • Selecting material composition
  • Defining crystal or molecular structures
  • Preparing simulation models

docs.title: Step 2: Structure Construction
docs.text:
Atomic structures are generated and prepared for computational simulation.

Tools:

  • Crystal structure database
  • Molecular builder
  • Structure optimization tools

docs.title: Step 3: First-Principles Calculation
docs.text:
First-principles calculations are performed to understand electronic properties from quantum mechanical principles.

Main approach:

Density Functional Theory (DFT)

Software:

Quantum ESPRESSO

Main calculations:

  • Geometry optimization
  • Electronic structure calculation
  • Charge analysis

docs.title: Step 4: Accelerated Atomistic Simulation
docs.text:
Large material systems require efficient simulation approaches.

This stage introduces:

Density Functional Tight Binding (DFTB+)

Applications:

  • Large-scale atomic simulation
  • Structural analysis
  • Dynamic behavior investigation

docs.title: Step 5: Machine Learning Potential
docs.text:
Artificial intelligence approaches accelerate materials simulation.

Topics include:

  • Machine learning potential
  • Atomic environment representation
  • AI-assisted simulation

Example:

MACE Machine Learning Potential

docs.title: Step 6: High Performance Computing
docs.text:
Computational materials simulations require significant computational resources.

HPC workflow includes:

  • Linux environment
  • Job submission
  • Parallel computation
  • Data management

docs.title: Final Goal
docs.text:
The complete workflow enables researchers to:

  • Predict material properties
  • Understand atomic mechanisms
  • Accelerate materials discovery
  • Reduce experimental trial and error

Structure ↓ Simulation ↓ Analysis ↓ Discovery
